extracted.intended_audience: general readers; writers, programmers, and legal practitioners seeking information on reusable text/templates
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive standards for creating and using reusable, prewritten text (boilerplate) across contexts such as contracts, form letters, programming, and mass communication. Covers what counts as boilerplate, appropriate minimal personalization, productivity benefits, and software/tools for managing templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate text (or simply boilerplate) is any written text (copy) that can be reused in new contexts or applications without significant changes to the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used about statements, contracts, and source code; the term is often used pejoratively to refer to clichéd or unoriginal writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate language / clause in contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: In contract law, 'boilerplate language' or 'boilerplate clause' describes the parts of a contract that are considered standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A standard form contract or boilerplate contract is one where terms and conditions are set by one party and the other party has little or no ability to negotiate, placing them in a 'take it or leave it' position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate in form letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate language may exist in pre-created form letters used to send similar communications repeatedly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sender typically personalizes these minimally, often by just adding their name or specific details to a pre-written greeting and body, making templates practical for mass communication or repetitive correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate code (programming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate code are sections of code that must be included in many places with little or no alteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boilerplate code is particularly salient when the programmer must include a lot of code for minimal functionality. Related is 'bookkeeping code' which is interleaved with business logic to keep data structures updated or handle secondary aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate text as a productivity tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate text functionality in word processing increases productivity by allowing frequently used phrases, sentences, or paragraphs to be saved and reused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This significantly reduces time for repetitive writing tasks and minimizes typing errors; used especially in office communication, customer service, and technical documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template software capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Special boilerplate software manages prefabricated text fragments and templates across systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such tools can manage complex text templates and combine them dynamically with variables (e.g., names, dates), and support workflows; examples cited include AutoHotkey and TextExpander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate statement (minimal-effort responses)
rubrics_metrics.description: A boilerplate statement or response is a message used with minimal effort for multiple different situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: standard voicemail messages such as 'Thank you for holding. Your call is very important to us.' (implying that such statements are reusable and minimally tailored).

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate as potentially clichéd/unoriginal
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate is often characterized negatively when it becomes clichéd or unoriginal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes the term is 'often used pejoratively to refer to clichéd or unoriginal writing,' signaling a quality tradeoff: reusability vs. originality and perceived authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical minimal personalization guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: When using boilerplate (e.g., form letters), the expected minimal personalization is to add identifying specifics like the sender's name or situation-specific details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This minimal personalization preserves efficiency while providing necessary context; omission can render communication impersonal or inappropriate for the recipient.
